subject: Accounting
title: Deductions and Taxable Income
description: A 60-second lesson on Deductions and Taxable Income.

hook.text: You earn $80,000 but only pay tax on $60,000. The magic? Deductions.

buildup.text: Deductions reduce your taxable income—the number your tax bill is actually calculated on.

discovery.text: Common deductions include mortgage interest, charitable donations, and student loan interest.

twist.text: Most people take the standard deduction because itemizing isn't worth it for smaller expenses.

climax.text: Understanding deductions is the simplest legal way to lower your tax bill every year.

punchline.text: Deductions shrink what the tax man sees.

details.summary: Tax deductions reduce your taxable income — the amount of income subject to tax — by allowing you to subtract certain qualified expenses like mortgage interest, charitable donations, and business costs before calculating what you owe.
details.whyItMatters: Deductions are the primary tool taxpayers use to legally reduce their tax bills, and understanding how they work is essential for effective personal and business financial planning.
takeaways: Deductions lower your taxable income, not your tax bill dollar-for-dollar
The standard deduction is a flat amount available to all taxpayers; itemizing lists individual deductions
Common deductions include mortgage interest, state taxes, charitable contributions, and business expenses

faq.question: How do tax deductions reduce what you owe?
faq.answer: Deductions lower your taxable income, the amount used to calculate your tax. If you earn $80,000 with $15,000 in deductions, you're taxed on $65,000. The actual savings depends on your marginal bracket — a deduction in the 22% bracket saves 22 cents per dollar deducted.

faq.question: Should I take the standard deduction or itemize?
faq.answer: Take whichever is larger. The standard deduction is a flat amount ($14,600 for single filers in 2024). If your total itemizable deductions — mortgage interest, state taxes, charitable gifts, etc. — exceed that amount, itemizing saves you more. Most taxpayers benefit from the standard deduction.
